I give up. I did not find a proof I could formalize, so I left `/work/combi_imosl_2015_c6.lean` unchanged.

The statement is ISL 2015 C6, and the difficult case is an infinite `S`. If `S` is finite, the result is easy: for any `N`, take `m = max N (∑ s ∈ S) + 1`. No subset of `S` sums to `m`, so `m` is not clean. I did not write that case up in Lean.

For infinite `S`, I tried the generating-function route. With `f(n)` the number of odd-size subsets of `S` summing to `n`, cleanness means `f(n) = 1` for all large `n`, and `∏(1+x^s) − ∏(1−x^s) = 2·F(x)`. I could not turn that into a contradiction. I also tried to find two distinct odd representations of the same large `n` by exchanging elements, and that did not produce one either. Formalizing the official argument would take a substantial development in Lean and Mathlib, which is beyond what I can reliably finish here.
